claims: Interstate 80 stretches roughly 2,900 miles from San Francisco, California, to Teaneck, New Jersey.
Interstate 80 traverses California, Nevada, Utah, Wyoming, Nebraska, Iowa, Illinois, Indiana, Ohio, Pennsylvania, and New Jersey.

San Francisco/Oakland CA, Sacramento CA, Reno NV, Salt Lake City UT, Cheyenne WY, Omaha NE, Des Moines IA, Joliet IL, Toledo OH, Cleveland OH, Youngstown OH, Sharon/Farrell PA, Stroudsburg PA, Paterson NJ, and Teaneck NJ (near New York City) are major cities along Interstate 80.
As of April 2026, ongoing construction for Express Lanes is occurring between Davis and Sacramento on Interstate 80 in California.
A 55-hour closure was scheduled for mid-April in San Francisco between 17th Street and Fourth Street on Interstate 80.
As of April 2026, a $22.5 million project is underway to build a new interchange in Gretna on Interstate 80 in Nebraska.
Interstate 80 in Wharton, New Jersey had a sinkhole closure in 2025.
As of April 2026, maintenance and repair projects continue on Interstate 80 in New Jersey following a 2025 sinkhole closure in Wharton.
Speed limits on Interstate 80 generally range from 55 mph in urban areas to 70-80 mph in rural sections, especially across the Midwest and West.
Interstate 80 passes near Lake Tahoe/Reno, the Great Salt Lake, the Missouri River, and the Delaware Water Gap.
John Deere is located along the Interstate 80 corridor.
Ford is located along the Interstate 80 corridor.
Tyson Foods is located along the Interstate 80 corridor.
